issue: The script hardcodes 'disadv == "70%"' as the condition for disadvantaged status. The data dictionary states that any non-empty value in the Disadv % column qualifies a project as disadvantaged, not specifically '70%'. This will incorrectly mark projects with other non-empty Disadv % values as 'No'.
suggestion: Change the condition to check for any non-empty/non-NA value: ifelse(!is.na(disadv) & str_squish(disadv) != "", "Yes", "No")

issue: The script sets funding_amount to project_cost when invited == 'Yes', but the data dictionary explicitly states Funding Amount is 'No Information' for Texas Year 0 (category: No Award Data Available). Assigning project_cost as a proxy for funding_amount is not supported by the dictionary.
suggestion: Set funding_amount = as.character(NA) or 'No Information' for all rows, consistent with the dictionary's 'No Award Data Available' category.

issue: The EC keyword matching uses 'ec_str' which is not defined anywhere in the script. This will cause a runtime error unless ec_str is defined in the global environment, which is fragile and undocumented.
suggestion: Define ec_str inline or as a local variable within the function containing all EC keywords from the dictionary: 'cyanotoxin|dioxane|emerging contaminant|lithium|manganese|Mn|Perfluoro-n-pentanoic acid|PFPeA|PFAS|PFOA|PFOS|trihalomethane|THM|Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule'.

issue: The lead keyword pattern uses 'lsl|lead' but the dictionary specifies 'lead' or 'LSLR' as the trigger keywords. 'lsl' is a partial match that could match unintended strings, and 'LSLR' is not explicitly included (though ignore.case covers it).
suggestion: Change the pattern to 'lead|lslr' with ignore.case = TRUE to match the dictionary specification more precisely.

issue: The script maps project_id from a column named 'pif' but the dictionary refers to the source column as 'PIF#' or 'PIF #'. Verify that after clean_names() the column is indeed named 'pif' and not 'pif_number' or similar.
suggestion: Confirm the cleaned column name from clean_names() matches 'pif'; if not, update the reference accordingly.

issue: project_cost is passed through clean_numeric_string() which likely returns a numeric or character type, but the script also uses project_cost directly (before mutation) in the funding_amount assignment. If clean_numeric_string modifies the type, the funding_amount assignment may inherit an unexpected type.
suggestion: Ensure the funding_amount line references the original raw project_cost column if needed, or reorder mutations to avoid dependency on a mutated column within the same mutate() call.

issue: The script checks `disadv == "70%"` for disadvantaged status, but the data shows three distinct values: "70%", "50%", and "30%". All three appear to represent valid disadvantaged percentages. Projects with 50% or 30% Disadv % will be incorrectly classified as "No".
suggestion: Change the condition to check for any non-NA/non-empty value in the disadv column, e.g., `ifelse(!is.na(disadv) & disadv != "", "Yes", "No")`, consistent with the data dictionary rule that any value in Disadv % means disadvantaged.

issue: The script references column `pif` after `clean_names()`, but the original column is named `PIF #`. After `clean_names()`, this becomes `pif_number` or `pif_` (with trailing special character handling), not `pif`. The column name contains a space and a `#` symbol which janitor may convert differently.
suggestion: Verify the exact column name produced by `clean_names()` for `PIF #` — it is likely `pif_number` or `pif_`. Use `names(tx_ppl)` to confirm and update the script accordingly.

issue: The raw data contains carriage returns (`\r`) embedded in string fields (e.g., `Sandbranch\rDevelopment & WSC`, multi-line Project Description values). `str_squish()` only collapses whitespace and spaces; it does not remove `\r` characters, leaving them embedded in cleaned strings.
suggestion: Add an explicit `str_replace_all(., "\r", " ")` or `str_replace_all(., "[\r\n]+", " ")` step before `str_squish()` for `borrower`, `project_description`, and `project_id` fields.

issue: The script checks `pwsid %in% c("", "Pending")` to replace with "No Information", but the raw `PWS ID` column also has `NA` values (1.8% NA per column summary). These NAs will not be caught by the `%in%` check and will remain as `NA` rather than "No Information".
suggestion: Add `is.na(pwsid)` to the condition: `ifelse(is.na(pwsid) | pwsid %in% c("", "Pending"), "No Information", pwsid)`.

issue: The script sets `funding_amount = ifelse(invited == "Yes", project_cost, "No Information")`. However, `project_cost` at this point has already been processed by `clean_numeric_string()` and is presumably numeric or a cleaned string. Mixing numeric project_cost values with the string "No Information" in one column via `ifelse` will coerce all values to character, which may be inconsistent with downstream numeric expectations.
suggestion: Ensure the column type is intentionally character, or use `NA` instead of "No Information" for non-funded rows if numeric type is needed. Document the intended type explicitly.

issue: The EC keyword list in the data dictionary includes terms like "trihalomethane", "THM", "dioxane", "lithium", "manganese", "Mn", "cyanotoxin", "Perfluoro-n-pentanoic acid", "PFPeA", "PFAS", "PFOA", "PFOS", "Unregulated Contaminant Monitoring Rule". The script uses a variable `ec_str` whose definition is not shown. If `ec_str` is missing any of these terms or is malformed, EC projects will be misclassified as General.
suggestion: Verify that `ec_str` contains all required keywords from the data dictionary and is constructed as a valid regex alternation string. Display or log `ec_str` for review.

issue: The Lead check uses `grepl("lsl|lead", ...)` but the data dictionary also lists "LSLR" as a trigger keyword. While "lsl" would match "LSLR" (case-insensitive), the pattern `lsl|lead` could also partially match unintended strings. Additionally, Lead check runs before EC check, so a project description mentioning both lead and an EC keyword would be classified as Lead only.
suggestion: Consider using word-boundary anchors or more specific patterns, and confirm the intended precedence between Lead and EC classifications in edge cases.

issue: The `Invited` column has 87.7% NA values and only 1 distinct non-NA value ("Yes"). The script uses `ifelse(invited == "Yes", "Yes", "No")` — NAs will evaluate to "No", which is the intended behavior per the data dictionary, but this should be explicitly verified rather than relying on NA coercion in `ifelse`.
suggestion: Consider using `ifelse(!is.na(invited) & invited == "Yes", "Yes", "No")` to make the NA handling explicit and self-documenting.

issue: Project Cost values in the raw data are formatted as currency strings with dollar signs and commas (e.g., `$2,300,000.00`, `$23,895,045.00`). The behavior of `clean_numeric_string()` is not shown; if it does not handle `$` and `,` removal, project_cost values will fail to parse correctly.
suggestion: Confirm `clean_numeric_string()` strips `$`, `,`, and `.00` or handles standard currency formatting before numeric conversion.

issue: The script applies `str_squish()` to `rank` and `points`, but these columns are numeric in the raw data (per column summary). `str_squish()` on a numeric column will first coerce to character, which may add unnecessary type ambiguity.
suggestion: Decide whether project_rank and project_score should be stored as numeric or character, and apply the appropriate conversion (e.g., `as.character(rank)` or `as.numeric(rank)`) explicitly rather than relying on `str_squish()`.
